1926, March
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 31
March 29th Hopelessness Brings Hope & Conversion: Joseph Guarnieri 24 re- ported hopelessly dying in Providence with complication - kidney trouble principally - is enrolled on St. Joseph's Day by his chum-friend "Edw'd" Kozak at the time a Russellite, who promises to do something specially pleasing to God, if his friend is spared. Two days later he phones that the patient is back to consciousness and able to talk. A week elapses and he phones his friend is actually reading the news-papers and feeling fine. Next day makes profession of faith, adjures heresy and returns after 7 years to reception of the Holy Sacraments. Thanks be to God. June 13th Both young men come to Mon- astery To-day healthy and happy. Thanks be to God.
Curviture of Spine & Paralisis Cured: Mildred Kirchoff (25) of 5737 Seminole had a bad fall when 9 years old. Four years later it began to affect her spine, leaving her badly deformed & para- lized. After doctring and suffering for seven years she was en- rolled in S.M.Assoc. in May last year. To-day, a picture of health, she is teaching in physical training school. Thanks be to God!
April 3rd Tripple Cause of Anxiety: Theodore Demanke 26, 7241 Wykes Ave. Detroit mentally deranged since the War 1918, now home from asylum where he was (at Aloyese) nine months, but not well at all. Joseph Demanke (39) drinks and blasphemes - Property to be sold - finally Sight threatened in eyes of Ann Demanke who enrolls all this evening for two years
April 14th Brain-Tumer. Marian Velten 13, of 1470 Helen Ave. ailing two years prepared yesterday in Hen. Ford's Hospital since last Tuesday - head shaven and on operating table for operation on Tumer of the Brain - her Brother Edward and her Father ready to give blood for "transfusion" if required in case she bled too freely. At this junctur the speaker for 9 doctors comes out and anounces a seeming change in location of tumer or possibly two tumers and therefore, "No operation To-day." She is enrolled this A.M. perpetually by poor anxious Mother - at 9.30 .... Next day Apr. 15th 7.15 p.m. Father & Brother report "Marion home To- day, Evidently improving. All hope now that no operation will be necessary. P.S. Oct. 7
